You are a developer community organizer preparing to attend China Tech Expo 2026, a technology conference held at the Qufu International Convention Center from March 13 to March 14, 2026. Your task is to research relevant technology topics by finding the most popular videos from a well-known short-form tech channel, plan your train travel from Beijing to Qufu and back, organize all information into a structured spreadsheet, document the complete plan in your team knowledge base, and add all key events to the shared calendar.

Begin by searching for the top 5 most-viewed videos from the Fireship channel on the video platform, sorted by popularity. For each video, retrieve the full title, view count, approximate duration in minutes, and a brief description of the key technologies discussed. Identify the primary technology topic covered in each video so you can prepare relevant knowledge before the conference sessions.

Next, look up the train station codes for Beijing South station and Qufu East station using the train booking system. Query available high-speed trains departing Beijing South and arriving at Qufu East on March 12, 2026. Select the most suitable after-work evening departure train for the outbound journey. Then query return trains from Qufu East to Beijing South on March 15, 2026, and select a suitable afternoon return train. Retrieve the intermediate stop information for both selected trains.

Check the shared calendar to see any existing events between March 12 and March 15, 2026, and note any potential conflicts.

Create an Excel workbook named Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx in your workspace. It must contain three sheets. The first sheet should be named Prep_Videos and contain columns: Rank, Title, Topic, View_Count, Duration_Min, and Key_Technologies. Populate it with the 5 videos you retrieved, ranked from most to least viewed. The second sheet should be named Travel_Details and contain columns: Leg, Train_No, From_Station, To_Station, Departure, Arrival, Duration_Min, Seat_Class, and Price_CNY. Add one row for the outbound journey and one row for the return journey, using the train codes and actual departure/arrival times you retrieved. Use first class for both legs and look up the actual price from the rail system for each leg. Record the station names and the seat class exactly as returned by the rail booking system (the system reports them in Chinese, e.g. 北京南 / 曲阜东 / 一等座) — do not translate them. The third sheet should be named Conference_Schedule and contain columns: Date, Time, Activity, Location, and Notes. Add at least six rows covering departure on March 12, conference day one sessions and activities on March 13, conference day two sessions and networking on March 14, and the return journey on March 15; the exact activities and times in this schedule are up to you. Write all cell values in the workbook as literal values (plain numbers and text) — do not use Excel formulas.

Create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Tech Conference Preparation - Qufu March 2026". The page should include a travel details section describing both train journeys with the actual train numbers, departure and arrival times, and station names you retrieved. It should also include a Learning Resources section listing the five video topics you identified, with a brief note on why each technology topic is relevant to conference preparation.

Finally, add the following events to the shared calendar: a travel event titled "Conference Travel: Beijing to Qufu" on March 12 from 17:00 to 20:00; a full-day conference event titled "Tech Conference Day 1" on March 13 from 09:00 to 18:00; a second full-day conference event titled "Tech Conference Day 2" on March 14 from 09:00 to 18:00; and a return travel event titled "Return: Qufu to Beijing" on March 15 from 14:30 to 17:30.

Configuration details for this task are provided in the file conference_config.json and general preparation guidelines are in prep_guide.md, both located in your workspace.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves with exactly four sub-agents. Video research and train planning are independent; after they return, the workbook and knowledge-base page can be written in parallel from one frozen plan.

Before Wave 1, dynamically resolve and read `conference_config.json` plus `prep_guide.md`. Freeze the channel, top-five ranking rule, station/date/seat preferences, conference schedule requirements, exact four calendar slots, and any conflict-handling guidance. Use `list_events` once for an ISO range covering 2026-03-12 through 2026-03-16 with a sufficiently large `maxResults`, then inspect title/time overlaps locally. In the same response that dispatches Wave 1, create only missing fixed events with `create_event` using exact ISO `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` values; retain every returned event ID.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 Explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one Explore sub-agent to own one complete read-only Fireship channel catalog session. Obtain the channel/video-list identifier, continue the returned list identifier with the platform's navigation cursor/page operation until source exhaustion, and retrieve details only as needed for complete title, integer view count, duration, description, and tags. Rank the whole observed catalog by view count descending with a stable Video_ID tie-break and return exactly the verified top five with rank, duration minutes, one evidence-supported primary topic, key technologies, and catalog page/row/duplicate controls. Do not stop after the first page or write artifacts.

   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 1): Use one Explore sub-agent to own the complete read-only travel branch. Resolve Beijing South and Qufu East station codes through the station lookup; query 2026-03-12 outbound and 2026-03-15 return tickets with the resolved codes; select a task-suitable after-work evening outbound and afternoon return by actual times, availability, and first-class (`一等座`) evidence; then retrieve intermediate stops for exactly those two selected train/date pairs. Return one compact two-leg table preserving actual Chinese station/seat labels, train numbers, timestamps, duration, first-class price, and stop-list/ticket coverage. Do not invent a price or translate returned labels.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates top-five order, two journey constraints, seat/price evidence, stop coverage, and calendar conflicts, then freezes one immutable conference-plan payload including at least six schedule rows.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 Coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole writer of `Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx`. Create the exact three sheets from the frozen payload with exact headers/order, five videos, two travel legs, at least six schedule rows, and literal values only. Read all sheets back and return path plus row/value checks.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one Coder sub-agent as the sole owner of the exact-title `Tech Conference Preparation - Qufu March 2026` page. Search exact title, create or complete one nonduplicate page with both actual train journeys and all five learning topics/relevance notes, retrieve it, and return ID plus coverage checks.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles train/video facts across both artifacts, retrieves each created/reused calendar event with `get_event(eventId)`, preserves unrelated conflicts, and verifies all original outputs without a third wave.

You are a read-only research sub-agent for a developer community organizer preparing for China Tech Expo 2026 (March 13-14, Qufu). Your ONLY job: find the top 5 most-viewed videos from the YouTube channel "Fireship" and return verified details. Do NOT write any files. Use ONLY the mcp__youtube__* tools.

Steps:
1. Locate the Fireship channel: use mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos with query "Fireship" (maxResults 20) and extract the channelId of the Fireship channel (title should be "Fireship"). Confirm with mcp__youtube__channels_getChannel (channelId) — verify the channel title contains "Fireship".
2. Start a full catalog listing: call mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos with the channelId and sortOrder "popular" (creates a list session; note the returned listId and the videos on page 1).
3. Exhaust the catalog: repeatedly call mcp__youtube__channels_navigateList with the listId and page numbers 2, 3, 4, ... until the platform reports no more videos / an end-of-list signal (all pages consumed). Track every video ID you see to detect duplicates; record total pages navigated and total unique videos observed. Do NOT stop after the first page.
4. Rank: from ALL observed videos, sort by view count descending. If the list responses include view counts, use them; otherwise call mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo for the highest-view candidates (parts such as snippet, contentDetails, statistics) to obtain the exact integer viewCount, duration (ISO 8601, e.g. PT8M32S), title, description, and tags. Get exact counts for the top ~10 candidates to safely confirm the top 5. Tie-break stably by video ID.
5. For each of the final top 5: compute Duration_Min as the duration rounded to the nearest whole minute (state your rounding rule), identify the PRIMARY technology topic (one short phrase, e.g. "AI/LLMs", "WebAssembly", "TypeScript", "Rust", "Cloud/Serverless", "Python", etc.) based on title/description/tags, and list 2-5 Key_Technologies (specific tools/frameworks/languages mentioned, e.g. GPT-4, LangChain, WASM, Deno, React, etc.).

Return ONLY this compact structured report (plain text):
- Channel name and channelId verified.
- Catalog controls: pages navigated, unique videos observed, duplicates found, ranking method.
- Table of the verified top 5, ranked most-viewed to least-viewed, with columns: Rank | Video_ID | Title (full) | View_Count (integer) | Duration_Min | Primary_Topic | Key_Technologies.
- One line of evidence per video (where the view count/duration came from).

Acceptance criteria: exactly 5 rows, sorted descending by integer view count, each with full title, integer view count, duration in minutes, one primary topic, and key technologies. If the platform's list cannot be fully exhausted, report exactly what you observed and why.
Fireship top-5 videos research

You are a read-only travel research sub-agent. A developer is attending China Tech Expo 2026 (March 13-14) at Qufu International Convention Center. Travel: outbound Beijing → Qufu on 2026-03-12 (after-work EVENING departure), return Qufu → Beijing on 2026-03-15 (AFTERNOON departure). Seat class: 一等座 (first class). Use ONLY the mcp__rail_12306__* tools. Do NOT write any files. Do NOT invent prices or times — only report what the system returns. Keep ALL Chinese labels exactly as returned (e.g. 北京南 / 曲阜东 / 一等座) — do NOT translate them.

Steps:
1. Resolve station codes: call mcp__rail_12306__get-station-code-by-names with stationNames "北京南|曲阜东" (fallback: get-station-code-of-citys "北京|曲阜"). Record the station_code for 北京南 and 曲阜东. (Do not pass Chinese names directly to ticket queries — always use the resolved codes.)
2. Outbound query (2026-03-12): call mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets with date "2026-03-12", fromStation=<北京南 code>, toStation=<曲阜东 code>, trainFilterFlags "G" (high-speed), limitedNum=20, and also a broader query if needed (e.g. no filter or "GD") to see all evening options. Identify the most suitable AFTER-WORK EVENING train: departs roughly 17:00-20:00, arrives the same evening, and has 一等座 availability WITH a price. Record: train_no + display train number, actual departure time, actual arrival time, duration, 一等座 price in CNY, the exact Chinese seat label (e.g. 一等座), and exact Chinese station names as returned (e.g. 北京南, 曲阜东), plus the telecodes for both stations from the ticket row.
3. Return query (2026-03-15): call mcp__rail_12306__get-tickets with date "2026-03-15", fromStation=<曲阜东 code>, toStation=<北京南 code>, trainFilterFlags "G", limitedNum=20 (broaden if needed). Select a suitable AFTERNOON return train (departs ~14:30 or later, arrives in the evening, ideally arriving before ~20:00), with 一等座 availability and price. Record the same fields as above, plus telecodes.
4. Intermediate stops for BOTH selected trains: call mcp__rail_12306__get-train-route-stations for each selected train using the full train_no (e.g. "240000G1xxxx"), fromStationTelecode and toStationTelecode from the ticket row, and departDate (2026-03-12 for outbound, 2026-03-15 for return). Record the COMPLETE stop list (every intermediate station with its arrival/departure times) for both legs.

Return ONLY this compact structured report (plain text):
- Station codes resolved: 北京南 → code, 曲阜东 → code.
- OUTBOUND leg: Train_No | From_Station (Chinese as returned) | To_Station (Chinese) | Departure (yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm) | Arrival | Duration_Min (computed from times) | Seat_Class (Chinese, e.g. 一等座) | Price_CNY (first-class, numeric) | availability evidence.
- RETURN leg: same fields.
- For each leg: the complete intermediate stop list (station name + arrive/depart times) and how many ticket rows the query returned (ticket coverage note).

Acceptance criteria: both legs selected from REAL query results with REAL 一等座 prices; outbound departs in the evening window (~17:00-20:00) on 2026-03-12; return departs in the afternoon on 2026-03-15; stop lists retrieved for exactly those two trains; no invented values; Chinese labels preserved verbatim.
Beijing-Qufu train planning

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-yt-12306-tech-conference-travel-notion-excel/workspace/Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx

IMPORTANT: keep the Chinese station names (北京南, 曲阜东) and seat class (一等座) EXACTLY as given — do not translate. Departure/Arrival are text strings. Duration_Min and Price_CNY are numbers.

=== Sheet 3: Conference_Schedule ===
Headers (row 1): Date | Time | Activity | Location | Notes
Rows (at least 6; use these 10):

2026-03-13 | 13:30-17:30 | Afternoon conference sessions | Qufu International Convention Center | Keynote & tech talks
2026-03-13 | 17:30-19:00 | Evening networking | Qufu International Convention Center | Meet exhibitors and speakers
2026-03-14 | 09:00-12:00 | Morning conference sessions | Qufu International Convention Center | China Tech Expo 2026 Day 2

Workflow: create the workbook, name the default sheet "Prep_Videos" (or create/rename sheets to match exactly), create "Travel_Details" and "Conference_Schedule", write all data, then READ BACK all three sheets (read_data_from_excel) and verify every header and every cell value matches the spec above exactly. Delete any extra default sheets.

Return ONLY: the absolute file path, the sheet names in order, the row/column counts per sheet, and a per-sheet confirmation that all headers and cell values match the frozen spec (note any discrepancy — there should be none).
Build Tech_Conference_Plan.xlsx

You are the sole owner of a Notion knowledge-base page for a team conference-prep plan. Use only mcp__notion__* tools.

GOAL: ensure exactly ONE page exists with the EXACT title: "Tech Conference Preparation - Qufu March 2026"

Steps:
1. Search first: call mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Tech Conference Preparation" (and if needed the full title) to find any existing page with this exact title. Also search to locate the team knowledge base parent — look for a page whose title suggests a knowledge base / wiki / team hub (e.g. contains "Knowledge Base", "Team", "Wiki", "KB", or a top-level workspace page from search results). If a page with the exact target title ALREADY exists, reuse it (do NOT create a duplicate) — complete/update its content as below. If it does not exist, create it with mcp__notion__API-post-page under the best available parent (prefer the team knowledge base page if found; otherwise a top-level page returned by search).
2. Page content — include at least these sections (use headings + paragraphs/bullets):
   - Heading: "Travel Details"
     * Outbound: Train G235, 2026-03-12, departs 北京南 (Beijing South) 17:30, arrives 曲阜东 (Qufu East) 19:16, duration 106 min, seat 一等座 (first class), price ¥174.5. Direct train, no intermediate stops.
     * Return: Train G236, 2026-03-15, departs 曲阜东 15:00, arrives 北京南 16:46, duration 106 min, seat 一等座, price ¥174.5. Direct train, no intermediate stops.
     * Keep the Chinese station/seat labels 北京南 / 曲阜东 / 一等座 verbatim.
   - Heading: "Learning Resources" — list the five Fireship video topics (ranked by view count) with a brief note on why each is relevant to conference preparation:
     1. AI/LLMs — "Big Tech in panic mode... Did DeepSeek R1 just pop the AI bubble?" (3,878,491 views) — relevant: conference AI track will cover LLM disruption and open-weight models.
     2. AI/LLMs — "This free Chinese AI just crushed OpenAI's $200 o1 model..." (3,115,193 views) — relevant: understanding Chinese open-source AI landscape before Expo sessions.
     3. Linux/OS — "100+ Linux Things you Need to Know" (2,891,861 views) — relevant: foundation knowledge for cloud/backend sessions and demos.
     4. Software bugs/engineering — "25 crazy software bugs explained" (2,496,715 views) — relevant: reliability/QA themes and failure-case discussions at the Expo.
     5. Cybersecurity/Cloud — "Some bad code just broke a billion Windows machines" (2,467,547 views) — relevant: incident-response and platform reliability topics in enterprise sessions.
     You may also add a short intro paragraph noting the conference: China Tech Expo 2026, Qufu International Convention Center, 2026-03-13 to 2026-03-14.
3. Retrieve the created/updated page (API-retrieve-a-page) and return its page ID.

Return ONLY: the page ID, the exact page title, the parent page title/ID it lives under, whether it was created or reused, and a coverage check confirming both sections (Travel Details with both legs; Learning Resources with all five topics) are present in the retrieved page.
Create Notion KB prep page
